title: The Invention of the Airplane
summary: How the Wright brothers used patient testing and experimentation to build the first flying machine capable of controlled, powered flight.
poll: The invention of the airplane changed how people travel more than almost any other invention in history.

versions.title: The Invention of the Airplane
versions.text:
Long ago, no one could fly. Some tried big balloons. Some tried gliders. Most tries did not work.

Two brothers had a big idea. They ran a bike shop. They watched how birds fly. They tried many tests.

The brothers were not alone. Other men had tried to fly. One man flew gliders but got hurt.

The brothers built a flying machine. It had wings and an engine. They tested it again and again.

One day, their plane flew. It flew for a few seconds. This was the first real flight!

Today, planes fly all the time. We can fly far away fast. We thank the Wright brothers for this gift.

Two brothers named Wilbur and Orville Wright had a bold idea, so they ran a small bicycle shop together in their quiet hometown, and they studied carefully how wild birds used their wings to glide, turn, and stay balanced in flight. They tried experiment after experiment, year after patient year, without ever giving up on their shared dream.

The Wright brothers were certainly not the only ones chasing this exact dream, since other inventors in several different countries had also attempted to build their own flying machines before them, often with very little success. versions.title: The Invention of the Airplane
versions.text:
Before airplanes ever existed at all, no human being could truly fly through the sky, and this seemed almost entirely impossible to most ordinary people living anywhere at that particular moment in human history. Some bold and adventurous inventors attempted enormous, floating hot-air balloons, whereas others attempted gliders with wide, aerodynamically curved wings, but most of these early, hopeful attempts simply did not succeed in the end at all, unfortunately.

Two brothers named Wilbur and Orville Wright had a bold and determined idea, so they instead operated a rather small, quite modest bicycle repair shop together in their quiet, thoroughly unremarkable hometown, and they spent countless patient hours closely studying how wild birds used their wings to glide, turn, and remain perfectly balanced during actual flight. They meticulously conducted experiment after each careful experiment, year after patient year, without ever once abandoning their shared, ambitious dream.

The Wright brothers were certainly not the only determined ones pursuing this ambitious and genuinely difficult dream, since other determined inventors in several different countries had also attempted, repeatedly and persistently, to construct and perfect their own flying machines before them, often with very little lasting success. One famous and talented glider pioneer flew often and remarkably skillfully for many years but was ultimately injured quite severely in a tragic, widely reported crash that shocked contemporary observers everywhere.

The brothers carefully and patiently designed and constructed their own experimental flying machine, complete with wide, carefully shaped wings and a small, remarkably lightweight engine of their own original design. They tested their machine repeatedly and meticulously, patiently fixing small problems each and every single time it failed to perform quite correctly as intended.

One famous winter day in December 1903, their machine actually lifted off the ground and flew, remaining airborne for only a brief handful of remarkably short seconds. This remarkable event was widely and rightly considered the very first genuinely real, fully controlled, powered flight in all of recorded human history. It fundamentally and permanently changed absolutely everything in aviation that followed soon afterward.

Today, airplanes fly every single day, all around us, safely and remarkably reliably carrying millions of passengers across the entire globe every single day. versions.title: The Invention of the Airplane
versions.text:
Before mechanized airplanes ever existed at all, no human being could truly and sustainably fly through the open sky, and this seemed almost entirely impossible to most ordinary people living anywhere at that particular moment in human history. Some bold and adventurous inventors attempted enormous, floating hot-air balloons, whereas others attempted unpowered gliders with wide, aerodynamically curved wings, but most of these early, hopeful attempts simply did not succeed in the end at all, unfortunately.

Two brothers named Wilbur and Orville Wright had a bold and remarkably determined idea, so they instead operated a rather small, quite modest bicycle repair shop together in their quiet, thoroughly unremarkable hometown in Ohio, and they spent countless patient hours closely studying how wild birds used their wings to glide, turn, and remain perfectly balanced during actual flight. They very meticulously conducted experiment after each careful experiment, year after patient year, without ever once abandoning their shared, ambitious dream.

The Wright brothers were certainly not the only determined ones pursuing this ambitious and genuinely difficult dream, since other determined inventors in several different countries had also attempted, repeatedly and persistently, to design, construct, and perfect their own flying machines before them, often with very little lasting success. One famous and talented glider pioneer flew often and remarkably skillfully for many years but was ultimately injured quite severely in a tragic, widely reported crash that shocked contemporary observers across the globe.

The brothers carefully and patiently designed and constructed their own experimental flying machine, complete with wide, carefully shaped wings and a small, remarkably lightweight engine entirely of their own original design. They tested their machine repeatedly and meticulously, patiently fixing small problems each and every single time it stubbornly failed to perform quite correctly as intended.

One famous and historic winter day in December of 1903, their machine actually lifted off the ground and flew, remaining airborne for only a brief handful of remarkably short, fleeting seconds. This remarkable event was widely and rightly considered the very first genuinely real, fully controlled, sustained, powered flight in all of recorded human history. It fundamentally and permanently changed absolutely everything in modern aviation that followed soon afterward.

Today, airplanes fly every single day, all around us, safely and remarkably reliably carrying millions upon millions of passengers across the entire globe every single day. We can thank the Wright brothers for initiating this truly enormous and genuinely lasting transformation in how human beings travel around the entire world, connecting distant and faraway places together like never truly before in all of human history.

HIGH.modelAnswer: The Wright brothers' breakthrough grew out of earlier, independent attempts at flight, including balloons and gliders, which showed that many pioneers shared the same ambitious dream despite repeated, sometimes painful failures. Working carefully in their own small bicycle shop, the brothers studied birds, designed their own flying machine, and ran experiment after experiment, patiently fixing small problems each time something failed to work correctly. Their eventual, carefully controlled, powered flight in 1903 proved that sustained human flight was truly possible, and that remarkable achievement eventually transformed travel entirely, leading to the fast, reliable air travel that billions of people now depend on every single day without a second thought.
